data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet for Albania summarizes students’ performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-olds. The creative thinking test contains 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. In Albania, the factsheet reports a mean creative thinking score of 13 on a 60-point scale, significantly below the OECD average (33), and provides proficiency-level distributions (e.g., 16% at Level 3 or above; 3% at Level 5 or 6). It also reports relationships between creative thinking and mathematics/reading performance (e.g., 35% of variance uniquely attributed to mathematics performance; correlations of 0.66 with mathematics and 0.58 with reading). The document further highlights within-Albania gaps by socioeconomic quartiles and gender, and reports associations between creative thinking and students’ beliefs/attitudes and school pedagogies, while noting COVID-19-related data collection challenges and the meaning of asterisks for countries/economies with weaker technical standards.
